category_description: Pay, leave and government payments for people who work in Canada.
subcategory_description: Government payments for people who are out of work, raising children or on a low income.
label: EI regular benefit rate
context: The basic share of average insurable weekly earnings. A family supplement can raise it for low-income families.

label: Maximum EI regular weekly benefit
context: Based on the maximum yearly insurable earnings. The weekly rate stays the same for the length of the claim.

label: Maximum weeks of EI regular benefits
context: The number of weeks depends on the regional rate of unemployment and on insurable hours.

label: Minimum weeks of EI regular benefits
context: The number of weeks depends on the regional rate of unemployment and on insurable hours.

label: Fewest insurable hours needed to qualify
context: The requirement falls with a higher regional rate of unemployment. It applies without a notice of violation.

label: Most insurable hours needed to qualify
context: The requirement is highest where the regional rate of unemployment is 6% or less. It applies without a notice of violation.

label: Net family income limit for the EI family supplement
context: Families with children who receive the Canada child benefit and have net family income at or below this amount may get the supplement. The supplement falls as income rises.

subject_intro: What EI regular benefits pay, how the weekly amount is worked out, how many weeks you can get, the hours you need and who is eligible.
